draft.title: Companies and limited liability
card: An incorporated business, or company, is a legal entity separate from its owners. It can own property, sign contracts, and sue or be sued in its own name.
The owners of a company are its shareholders. Their liability is limited: if the company fails, they can lose only the money they put in, not their own homes or savings.
has Pty Ltd after its name. It cannot sell shares to the general public, so its shares are often held by a family or a few owners.
has Ltd after its name. It can sell shares to the public to raise money, and many are listed on the ASX (Australian Securities Exchange).
draft.remember: A company stands apart from its shareholders, so they risk only what they put in.

a.q: Chen bought $5,000 of shares in a company. It collapses owing $2 million. What is the most Chen can lose?
opts: The $5,000 he put into the company
A share of the full $2 million debt
His house and savings, if the debt needs it
Nothing, as only the company's managers pay
a.why: Shareholders have limited liability, so Chen can lose only the $5,000 he put in. The debt belongs to the company, a separate legal entity, so he does not take on a share of it and his own assets are safe.
a.clue: Whose debt is the $2 million: Chen's or the company's?

b.q: Greenleaf Pty Ltd, a Ballarat nursery, wants to raise money by selling shares to the public on the ASX. What must happen first?
opts: It must become a public company (Ltd)
Nothing, a Pty Ltd can already sell shares publicly
Its owners must accept unlimited liability
It must stop being an incorporated business
b.why: Only a public company can sell shares to the public, so Greenleaf must change from Pty Ltd to Ltd. It does not give up limited liability or incorporation, because a public company is still a company and its shareholders still risk only what they put in.
b.clue: What do the letters Pty Ltd tell you about who can buy shares?

a.best: The $5,000 he put into the company

b.best: It must become a public company (Ltd)
